primary.poolable_reason: THE POOL STANDS, AND EVERY STEP OF IT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. THE ESTIMAND IS THE SAME IN ALL THREE REGISTRATIONS. ORION-9 registers 'Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510'; ORION-10 and ORION-11 register 'Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510'. Same quantity, same anchor, same day, all three analysed by ANCOVA and reported by the registry as a 'Mean Difference (Final Values)'. THE ONLY DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE THREE STRINGS IS 'Percent' AGAINST 'Percentage' -- orthography, which is precisely the trap that has manufactured false disagreements in this repository before, and it is not one here. ALL THREE PER-TRIAL VALUES ARE THE REGISTRY'S OWN, DIGIT FOR DIGIT: ORION-9 -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), ORION-10 -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), ORION-11 -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). ALL THREE ARM PAIRS SUM TO THEIR REGISTRATION'S RECORDED ENROLMENT EXACTLY: 242+240=482, 781+780=1561, 810+807=1617. ARM LABELS AND ROLES ARE CORRECT ON ALL THREE. AND THE POOLED VALUE REPRODUCES: REML inverse-variance random effects on the three mean differences gives -54.0014 (-58.1652 to -49.8377), which is what the object holds and what the index card publishes, to four decimal places. THE CARD, THE OBJECT AND THE INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION ALL AGREE.  [RESTATED 2026-08-20. This sentence was written while the pool was fitted with DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates. It is now REML, under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The estimate moved from -54.00144508917459 (-58.16516691761607 to -49.83772326073311) to -53.97 (-58.3 to -49.64) and tau-squared from 9.524722803298308 to 10.595364. The original wording is beside this under poolable_reason_superseded_2026_08_20 -- a sentence that recorded a decision is restated, never deleted.]

sensitivity.method: leave-one-out, plus a comparison of between-study variance estimators
sensitivity.authority: Cochrane Handbook version 6.5.1, section 10.10.4.4: methods other than DerSimonian and Laird estimate the between-study variance better, and restricted maximum likelihood is the RevMan default. Section 10.14 governs the leave-one-out half. Cited to 10.10.4.4 rather than 10.10.4.5 because 10.10.4.5 is about INTERPRETATION with few studies and the method it compares is the confidence interval, not the variance estimator -- a miscitation this repository has already made once and corrected.
sensitivity.decision_under_test: Two decisions. First, whether the pooled reduction depends on any single trial. Second, whether it depends on the between-study variance estimator and interval method -- which at k=3, with the house rule against REML below k=10, is not a formality but the reason this table exists. sensitivity.conclusion: NO SINGLE TRIAL CARRIES THIS RESULT. Omitting each in turn gives -55.56 (-59.62 to -51.50), -52.18 (-55.85 to -48.51) and -53.90 (-61.84 to -45.97). All three exclude no effect and the pooled point moves by at most 1.8 percentage points on a scale of 54.

between_study_variance_method_comparison.verdict: IT DID NOT. The point estimate spans -53.95 to -53.97 across all six combinations -- a range of five hundredths on a scale of fifty-four -- and every one of the six intervals excludes no effect, the widest by more than forty percentage points. THE INTERVAL, NOT THE POINT, IS WHAT THE METHOD CHANGES: Wald gives about -58 to -50 and Hartung-Knapp about -64 to -44, roughly twice the width. At k=3 with I-squared of 72 per cent, HARTUNG-KNAPP IS THE HONEST ONE, and the precision shown on the index card is optimistic even though its direction and magnitude are not in doubt. pooled.caveats: WHAT A READER SHOULD KNOW ANYWAY, NONE OF WHICH OVERTURNS THE ESTIMATE. (1) THE ESTIMATOR IS NOT THIS PROJECT'S OWN STANDARD FOR THIS k. REML underestimates between-study variance when k is small, and the house rule is REML or REML below k=10. This pool is k=3. IT WAS RECOMPUTED UNDER BOTH: REML gives -53.95 (-58.40 to -49.51) with tau-squared 11.36, REML gives -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64) with tau-squared 10.60, against DL's -54.00 (-58.17 to -49.84) with tau-squared 9.52. The point estimate moves by five hundredths of a percentage point on a scale of fifty-four. THE CHOICE OF ESTIMATOR DOES NOT CHANGE THIS ANSWER, and the published value is retained rather than re-rounded, because moving a correct published number by 0.05 would break every reader's record for no gain. Whether the corpus headline should move to REML everywhere is a display-change policy question, not a finding about this topic. (2) HETEROGENEITY IS HIGH AND k IS SMALL: Q = 7.14 on 2 degrees of freedom, I-squared 72 per cent. A Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest one at this k, is -63.71 to -44.30 -- MUCH WIDER than the Wald interval on the card. The direction and the magnitude are not in doubt; the PRECISION on the card is optimistic. (3) THE THREE POPULATIONS ARE NOT THE SAME: ORION-9 enrolled heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, ORION-10 atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, ORION-11 ASCVD or risk-equivalents. That is a real clinical difference and the most likely source of the heterogeneity above. It is not an estimand difference -- all three measured the same thing on different people -- but it is why a single number should not be read as applying uniformly to all three groups. (4) LDL-C PERCENT CHANGE IS A SURROGATE. This review pools a laboratory value, not an event. Nothing here estimates an effect on death, myocardial infarction or stroke, and no such claim should be read into it. (5) ONE STORED INTERVAL BOUND IS RECONSTRUCTED RATHER THAN READ: ORION-11's upper limit is held as -50.34 where the registry prints -50.35, a rounding artefact of recomputing the interval from a point estimate and a standard error. One hundredth of a percentage point, recorded because a reader comparing the two should not have to wonder whether it means something.  [RESTATED 2026-08-20: this pool is now fitted with REML under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere.", so the caveat that its estimator was not this project's standard for its k no longer applies. The sentence is kept, restated, rather than deleted, because a reader who saw the old one should be able to see what became of it.]
pooled.card_note: endpoint definitions read and CONFIRMED identical in all three registries, every value matches the registry; but I² 72% on k=3, so the Hartung-Knapp interval −63.7 to −44.3 is the honest one
pooled.caveats_superseded_2026_08_20: WHAT A READER SHOULD KNOW ANYWAY, NONE OF WHICH OVERTURNS THE ESTIMATE. (1) THE ESTIMATOR IS NOT THIS PROJECT'S OWN STANDARD FOR THIS k. DerSimonian-Laird underestimates between-study variance when k is small, and the house rule is REML or Paule-Mandel below k=10. This pool is k=3. IT WAS RECOMPUTED UNDER BOTH: Paule-Mandel gives -53.95 (-58.40 to -49.51) with tau-squared 11.36, REML gives -53.97 (-58.30 to -49.64) with tau-squared 10.60, against DL's -54.00 (-58.17 to -49.84) with tau-squared 9.52. The point estimate moves by five hundredths of a percentage point on a scale of fifty-four. THE CHOICE OF ESTIMATOR DOES NOT CHANGE THIS ANSWER, and the published value is retained rather than re-rounded, because moving a correct published number by 0.05 would break every reader's record for no gain. Whether the corpus headline should move to REML everywhere is a display-change policy question, not a finding about this topic. (2) HETEROGENEITY IS HIGH AND k IS SMALL: Q = 7.14 on 2 degrees of freedom, I-squared 72 per cent. A Hartung-Knapp interval, which is the honest one at this k, is -63.71 to -44.30 -- MUCH WIDER than the Wald interval on the card. The direction and the magnitude are not in doubt; the PRECISION on the card is optimistic. (3) THE THREE POPULATIONS ARE NOT THE SAME: ORION-9 enrolled heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, ORION-10 atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, ORION-11 ASCVD or risk-equivalents. That is a real clinical difference and the most likely source of the heterogeneity above. It is not an estimand difference -- all three measured the same thing on different people -- but it is why a single number should not be read as applying uniformly to all three groups. (4) LDL-C PERCENT CHANGE IS A SURROGATE. This review pools a laboratory value, not an event. Nothing here estimates an effect on death, myocardial infarction or stroke, and no such claim should be read into it. (5) ONE STORED INTERVAL BOUND IS RECONSTRUCTED RATHER THAN READ: ORION-11's upper limit is held as -50.34 where the registry prints -50.35, a rounding artefact of recomputing the interval from a point estimate and a standard error. One hundredth of a percentage point, recorded because a reader comparing the two should not have to wonder whether it means something.
pooled.stands_because_superseded_2026_08_20: THE POOL STANDS, AND EVERY STEP OF IT WAS CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. THE ESTIMAND IS THE SAME IN ALL THREE REGISTRATIONS. ORION-9 registers 'Percent Change in LDL-C From Baseline To Day 510'; ORION-10 and ORION-11 register 'Percentage Change in LDL-C From Baseline to Day 510'. Same quantity, same anchor, same day, all three analysed by ANCOVA and reported by the registry as a 'Mean Difference (Final Values)'. THE ONLY DIFFERENCE BETWEEN THE THREE STRINGS IS 'Percent' AGAINST 'Percentage' -- orthography, which is precisely the trap that has manufactured false disagreements in this repository before, and it is not one here. ALL THREE PER-TRIAL VALUES ARE THE REGISTRY'S OWN, DIGIT FOR DIGIT: ORION-9 -49.52 (-55.04 to -43.99), ORION-10 -57.64 (-60.86 to -54.43), ORION-11 -53.50 (-56.66 to -50.35). ALL THREE ARM PAIRS SUM TO THEIR REGISTRATION'S RECORDED ENROLMENT EXACTLY: 242+240=482, 781+780=1561, 810+807=1617. ARM LABELS AND ROLES ARE CORRECT ON ALL THREE. AND THE POOLED VALUE REPRODUCES: DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance random effects on the three mean differences gives -54.0014 (-58.1652 to -49.8377), which is what the object holds and what the index card publishes, to four decimal places. THE CARD, THE OBJECT AND THE INDEPENDENT RECOMPUTATION ALL AGREE.

primary.poolable_DEPRECATED_note: `poolable` MEANT ONLY 'the source page pooled these trials'. It was never a judgement that the pool was sound, and the renderer read it as permission to assert 'pooled on the X scale'. RENAMED to source_page_pooled, which is what it says. `poolable` is retained so nothing breaks, and it is DEPRECATED: read source_page_pooled for what the source did, and estimand_established for whether the pool is defensible. A PAGE SHOULD DISPLAY A POOLED ESTIMATE BECAUSE ITS ESTIMAND WAS ESTABLISHED, NOT BECAUSE SOMEONE ONCE POOLED IT.
primary.estimand_established_means: TRUE only where every contributing trial has been READ and shown to measure the same quantity, or the same construct with a variance stated. FALSE where that was checked and failed. NULL where it was never checked -- AN ABSENT ASSERTION AND A NEGATIVE ONE ARE DIFFERENT STATES and null is not a pass.

display_change_announced.what_changed: `heterogeneity.i2` and `heterogeneity.tau2` are field names that each map to more than one standard definition. Every number is unchanged; each now carries the definition it holds. tau2's definition was already recoverable from the declared `estimator` beside it and is copied, never inferred. i2's was not recoverable and is DECIDED BY RECOMPUTING BOTH FORMS from this object's own per-trial inputs, with the evidence recorded.
display_change_announced.why: A reader recomputing Higgins I-squared from the Q printed beside it would have concluded the object was wrong -- and would have been behaving exactly as we want readers to behave. An ambiguous label on an unambiguous number is a defect specifically against the only reader we claim to serve.

display_change_announced.what_changed: This pool was fitted with DerSimonian-Laird inverse-variance on extracted effect estimates. It is refitted with REML under DECISIONS-COCHRANE-2026-08-18.md section 1, on Cochrane Handbook 6.5 section 10.10.4.4: "Decision: REML, everywhere." The old fit was reproduced against the stored value FIRST (REPRODUCED) and only then replaced. Stored values are also rounded at storage -- effects to 4 decimals, tau-squared and Q to 6, I-squared to 4 -- because several of these pools carried sixteen significant figures on a two- or three-study pool.
display_change_announced.why: The corpus held two estimator conventions at once: 23 pools REML, 9 DerSimonian-Laird, 1 Paule-Mandel. Handbook 6.5 s10.10.4.4 records REML as RevMan's own current default and this project's statistics rules already refused DerSimonian-Laird below k=10, which every pool in this corpus is. The decision was taken on 2026-08-18 and not applied; applying it to some pools and not others would have been worse than either convention.

display_change_announced.why: A pooled estimate published without any comparison against the literature cannot be checked by a reader against anything, and P46 asks for the comparison to carry a DENOMINATOR so that a table of failures cannot pass as a survey.
display_change_announced.what_it_found: One error, and it is OURS: all three ORION trials register two co-primary LDL endpoints and this review's selection between them -- consistently the day-510 one -- is nowhere recorded. It is also the leading candidate for the one unresolved divergence, against a 2020 synthesis of what the arithmetic says are these same three trials.

published_comparison._why: Three trials, one drug, one endpoint, and every per-trial value posted by the registry -- so the trial-by-trial half of this comparison is complete in a way it cannot be where trials post no results. THE ERROR FOUND IS OURS and it is in the table below with the same weight as anything found in the literature.

reviews.citation: Khan SA, Naz A, Qamar Masood M, Shah R. Meta-Analysis of Inclisiran for the Treatment of Hypercholesterolemia. Am J Cardiol 2020;134:69-73. doi 10.1016/j.amjcard.2020.08.018
reviews.how_it_differs_from_ours: By arithmetic and timing it pools THIS REVIEW'S OWN THREE TRIALS -- its n of 3,660 is exactly their summed arm counts, and it was published five months after they reported. Its -51% (48 to 53) against this review's -53.97% is therefore a difference in EXTRACTION OR ENDPOINT rather than in trial set, which is what makes it the most informative row here.

reviews.citation: Imran TF, et al. PCSK9 inhibitors and small interfering RNA therapy for cardiovascular risk reduction: a systematic review and meta-analysis. PLoS One 2023;18(12):e0295359. doi 10.1371/journal.pone.0295359
reviews.scope: inclisiran 284 mg, reported separately from the PCSK9 antibodies
reviews.how_it_differs_from_ours: Four inclisiran studies rather than three, across a broader population. Lands within one percentage point of this review.

reviews.citation: Alaiz AR, et al. Inclisiran: Efficacy in Real World -- Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis. J Clin Med 2025;14(12):4163. doi 10.3390/jcm14124163
reviews.how_it_differs_from_ours: A different DESIGN, not a different trial set: single-arm observational change against a randomised placebo-corrected difference. It cannot confirm or contradict this review and is listed so the reader knows the question was asked.

reviews.citation: Burnett H, et al. Comparative efficacy of non-statin lipid-lowering therapies in patients with hypercholesterolemia at increased cardiovascular risk: a network meta-analysis. Curr Med Res Opin 2022;38(5):777-784. doi 10.1080/03007995.2022.2049164
reviews.scope: network meta-analysis placing inclisiran against evolocumab, alirocumab, bempedoic acid and ezetimibe
reviews.how_it_differs_from_ours: A different QUESTION -- relative efficacy between active agents, not the size of the effect against placebo. Its own reported heterogeneity is 'roughly equivalent to variation of 5-10% change in LDL-C', which is larger than the gap between this review and Khan 2020.

checks.detail: Khan et al. 2020 report LDL-C lowered by 51% (48 to 53) over 3 RCTs with 3,660 patients. This review's three trials sum to 3,660 participants, and the trials were published five months before that paper, so its trial set is almost certainly this one -- BUT THAT IS ARITHMETIC AND TIMING, NOT A READ TRIAL LIST, and it is recorded as such. This review reports -53.97% (-58.30 to -49.64). The intervals overlap and neither result changes the reading, but the point estimates differ by about three percentage points. The leading candidate is the co-primary endpoint above: their value may be the time-adjusted day 90 to 540 endpoint where ours is day 510. THAT CANNOT BE DECIDED FROM AN ABSTRACT, so it is left unresolved rather than explained.

A broader trial set including ORION-1 and a larger population, landing within one percentage point of this review's point estimate with heavily overlapping intervals.

checks.detail: Alaiz et al. 2025 pool 7 real-world studies with 1,454 patients and report a 42.77%% reduction (37.42 to 48.12), and attribute the gap against trial estimates to baseline LDL-C differences and real-world adherence. THIS IS NOT A CHECK ON EITHER NUMBER: a randomised placebo-corrected percent change and a single-arm observational change are different quantities, and neither can confirm the other. It is listed because a reader asking 'does this hold in practice' is asking a question THIS REVIEW DOES NOT ANSWER, and the honest response is to name the study that does and say why it is not comparable.
checks.quote: an average c-LDL reduction of 42.77% (95% CI: 37.42-48.12%)

divergence_decomposed.ours: Mean difference -53.97% (-58.30 to -49.64) in LDL-C percent change from baseline to day 510, k=3, random effects, REML.
divergence_decomposed.theirs: -51% (48 to 53) over what is by arithmetic the same three trials; -54.83% (-59.04 to -50.62) over four; -42.77% (37.42 to 48.12) over seven real-world cohorts; and a network analysis reporting relative rather than absolute effect.
divergence_decomposed.why_they_differ: NOT BY TRIAL SET, which is the unusual and useful thing about this comparison. The closest synthesis pools the same three trials and differs by about three percentage points, so the difference is in extraction or in WHICH REGISTERED CO-PRIMARY was taken -- day 510, or time-adjusted day 90 to 540. This review's own selection between those two is consistent across all three trials and was never recorded, which is the error listed above. The broader syntheses agree with this review closely; the real-world pooling does not, and its own authors attribute that to baseline LDL-C and adherence rather than to either estimate being wrong.

denominator.statement: 9 checks were applied and 6 came back clean, 1 found an error, 1 found something absent and 1 could not be settled at the layer available. The denominator is stated because a list of only the failures is not a finding, it is a selection.
denominator.symmetry: Confirmations are listed in the same table, in the same detail, as errors. THE ONE ERROR FOUND IS OURS -- an unrecorded selection between two registered co-primary endpoints -- and the published literature is implicated in none of the rows. That is the same result every cardiology topic reconciled in this corpus has produced, and a comparison with room only for their errors could not have found it out.
denominator.what_this_denominator_does_not_cover: The 51 records the screen retrieved and did not read. The check count is honest about the checks; the SCREEN is separately honest about its own size in the appraisal file, and neither number should be read as the other.
